title_en: Guizhou Province Electronic United Kangle Company v. Guiyang City Urban Planning Bureau — dispute over administrative decision on demolition of illegal building
keywords_en: Administrative; Urban Planning Administration; Second Instance; High People's Court; Guizhou Province; Legal Person; Urban Planning Law of the People's Republic of China; Guizhou Province's Implementation Measures for the Urban Planning Law of the People's Republic of China; Identification of Illegal Buildings; Legality of Demolition Penalty; Whether Seriously Affecting Urban Planning; Affirm the Original Judgment; Construction Without Permit; Illegal Building; Urban Planning Area; Administrative Litigation
full_text_en:
Guizhou Provincial Electronic United Kangle Company v. Guiyang City Urban Planning Bureau — dispute over administrative decision to demolish illegal building

Plaintiff: Guizhou Provincial Electronic United Kangle Company.

Legal representative: Chen Dezhong, General Manager.

Agents ad litem: Zhao Yongkang and Gao Yuming, cadres of Guizhou Provincial Administrative Economic Legal Service Center.

Defendant: Guiyang City Urban Planning Bureau, Guizhou Province.

Legal representative: Ma Wenfeng, Director.

Agents ad litem: Zhang Genxiang and Shen Maji, lawyers of Guiyang No. 3 Law Firm.

The plaintiff, Guizhou Provincial Electronic United Kangle Company, dissatisfied with the decision made by the defendant, Guiyang City Urban Planning Bureau, to demolish its illegal building, filed an administrative lawsuit with the Guiyang Intermediate People's Court.

Plaintiff's Allegations: The defendant's decision ordering the plaintiff to demolish the illegal building within a specified period was based on unclear facts and erroneous application of laws and regulations. The plaintiff's newly constructed Children's Paradise Building had been approved in principle by the Guiyang City Urban Management Committee and had been submitted to the defendant for examination and approval. Although the construction procedures for the project were incomplete, it did not constitute a serious violation of urban planning. The plaintiff requested the court to revoke the defendant's decision to demolish the building within a specified period. During the trial, the plaintiff also amended its claim, requesting the court to change the demolition decision to a fine and to allow the building to be retained.

The defendant, Guiyang City Urban Planning Bureau, did not submit any defense.

Facts Found by the Court: In early August 1992, the plaintiff intended to construct a Children's Paradise Building on the west side of the southern end of Ruijin North Road, a main thoroughfare in Guiyang City, and applied to the Guiyang City Urban Management Committee and the Yunyan District Urban Management Committee. The city and district committees respectively issued opinions stating "approval in principle, please provide support from the Planning Bureau, finalize the plan, and handle the procedures." The plaintiff submitted the construction plan to the defendant for examination and approval. Without the defendant's approval and without obtaining a Construction Project Planning Permit, the plaintiff commenced construction of the Children's Paradise Building without authorization on August 23 of the same year. On December 9 of the same year, the defendant, together with relevant responsible persons from the city and district urban management committees, went to the construction site and ordered the plaintiff to stop construction immediately and submit a written self-criticism. The plaintiff submitted a written self-criticism to the defendant on the same day, expressing willingness to cease construction and accept handling. However, the plaintiff did not stop construction.

On February 20, 1993, the defendant, pursuant to Articles 32 and 40 of the Urban Planning Law of the People's Republic of China, and Articles 23 and 24 of the Implementation Measures of Guizhou Province for the Urban Planning Law of the People's Republic of China, issued a decision to demolish the illegal building, ordering the plaintiff to dismantle the unfinished illegally constructed Children's Paradise Building on its own before March 7, 1993. The plaintiff, dissatisfied, applied for administrative reconsideration to the Guizhou Provincial Department of Urban and Rural Construction and Environmental Protection. On April 7, 1993, the Guizhou Provincial Department of Urban and Rural Construction and Environmental Protection upheld the decision of the Guiyang City Urban Planning Bureau to demolish the illegal building. During the period of reconsideration, the plaintiff continued construction, resulting in the main structure of the six-story building with a total floor area of 1,730 square meters being substantially completed.

The above facts were verified through court investigation and were not disputed by either party.

Opinion of the Court: Although the plaintiff's new Children's Paradise Building had been approved in principle by the urban management department and the plaintiff had applied to the defendant for relevant construction planning procedures, the fact that construction commenced without obtaining a Construction Project Planning Permit violated Article 32 of the Urban Planning Law of the PRC, which provides that "a construction unit or individual may only apply for commencement procedures after obtaining a Construction Project Planning Permit and other relevant approval documents." This constituted an illegal building. The Guiyang City Urban Planning Bureau's decision to order the demolition of the illegal building within a specified period was not improper. Given that the illegal building is located on the side of a main thoroughfare in Guiyang's urban area, which is an important area within the urban planning zone, and that the unauthorized commencement of construction of a permanent building without approval from the planning department in itself seriously affected the overall planning of the area, and that the plaintiff continued construction even after the defendant's intervention and issuance of the penalty decision, this constituted an aggravating circumstance under the Implementation Measures of Guizhou Province for the Urban Planning Law of the PRC and the Guiyang City Urban Construction Planning Management Measures. Therefore, the plaintiff's argument that the building did not constitute a serious impact on urban planning and its request to change the defendant's demolition decision to a fine and retention of the building were not supported. Pursuant to Article 54, Paragraph (1) of the Administrative Procedure Law of the PRC, the court rendered the following judgment on May 21, 1993: Affirm the decision of the Guiyang City Urban Planning Bureau to demolish the illegal building.

Judgment: After the first-instance verdict was announced, the plaintiff, Guizhou Provincial Electronic United Kangle Company, appealed to the Guizhou High People's Court on the grounds that "the facts found in the original judgment were unclear and the application of law was erroneous," requesting the court to quash the original judgment and instead enter a judgment imposing a fine and allowing the building to be retained, as well as to complete the construction procedures retroactively. The defendant, Guiyang City Urban Planning Bureau, submitted a response arguing that the first-instance judgment had clear findings of fact, correct application of laws and regulations, and conformed to legal procedures, and should be affirmed according to law.

During the second-instance proceedings in the Guizhou High People's Court, on October 20, 1993, the appellant, Guizhou Provincial Electronic United Kangle Company, voluntarily stated: "We will comply with and execute the first-instance judgment of the Guiyang Intermediate People's Court and apply to withdraw the appeal." Upon review, the Guizhou High People's Court found that the fact of the appellant's serious illegal construction of the Children's Paradise Building without a permit existed, and the appellee's penalty decision to demolish the illegal building was lawful. The appellant voluntarily applied to withdraw the appeal. Pursuant to Article 51 of the Administrative Procedure Law, the court issued a ruling on November 1, 1993: Permitting the appellant, Guizhou Provincial Electronic United Kangle Company, to withdraw the appeal. The parties shall execute the first-instance judgment of the Guiyang Intermediate People's Court.

By February 1994, the Children's Paradise Building illegally constructed by Guizhou Provincial Electronic United Kangle Company had been completely demolished.
